'''Victor Alexander Vyssotsky''' (February 26, 1931 – December 24, 2012) was an American [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]]. He is best known for his work on [[Multics]] and for co-creating ''[[Darwin (video game)|Darwin]]'', the first [[programming game]].

==Life and career==
Victor Alexander Vyssotsky was born on February 26, 1931, in [[Charlottesville, Virginia]], to astronomers [[Alexander Vyssotsky|Alexander]] and [[Emma Vyssotsky]] ({{nee}} Williams).<ref name=obit /><ref name=r1 />

He was the technical head of the [[Multics]] project at [[Bell Labs]] and later executive director of Research in the Information Systems Division of AT&T Bell Labs. Multics directly inspired [[Ken Thompson (computer programmer)|Ken Thompson]] to develop [[Unix]].<ref name=r2 /> Later, Vyssotsky was the founding director of Digital's Cambridge Research Lab.

Vyssotsky co-created the BLODI Block Diagram Compiler in 1960 at Bell Labs.<ref>[https://ethw.org/Bell_Telephone_Laboratories,_Inc._List_of_Significant_Innovations_&_Discoveries_(1925–1983) Bell Telephone Laboratories, Inc. List of Significant Innovations & Discoveries (1925–1983)]. ethw.org</ref> In 1961, together with [[Robert Morris (cryptographer)|Robert Morris]] and [[Douglas McIlroy]], he co-created ''[[Darwin (video game)|Darwin]]'', the first [[programming game]],<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Platform for massive multiplayer programming games |last=Ramón Jiménez |first=Héctor |date=2016-01-21 |access-date=2026-08-27 |degree=Bachelor |publisher=[[Polytechnic University of Catalonia]] |url=https://hdl.handle.net/2117/82314 |page=5 |quote=In 1961, Victor Vyssotsky, a mathematician and computer scientist working at Bell Labs, along with Robert Morris Sr. and Doug McIlroy, created Darwin [23]: the first programming game.}}</ref> on an [[IBM 7090]] at Bell Labs.<ref>[https://corewar.co.uk/darwin.htm Darwin]. corewar.co.uk</ref>

Vyssotsky died on December 24, 2012, in [[Orleans, Massachusetts]].
